L15: ### 動物の未来を変える、新しいがん治療の開発
L16: 
L17: MESSAGE
L18: ## ごあいさつ
L19: 
L20: どうぶつトランスレーショナルリサーチセンター（略称 iCAT）は、埼玉県所沢市の日本小動物医療センター附属の研究施設です。
L21: 
L22: 動物のがんの克服を目指して、がんについて基礎から臨床までさまざまな角度から研究しています。iCATは、水野拓也と伊賀瀬雅也が運営しており、大学と同等の水準で研究を実施しています。
L23: 
L24: またiCATは、日本小動物がんセンターに併設されているため、がんに関蓮するさまざまな臨床試験や実際の症例組織を用いた解析などを実施しやすい環境が整っております。
L25: 
L26: iCATでは、大学院生として博士号を取得することが可能です。また、臨床現場で働いている獣医師の方々が社会人大学院生として博士号を取得することも支援しています。さらに、関東の獣医系大学からの外部研修生（学部学生・大学院生）に対する研究指導も積極的に行っています。

L28: ### Para ensayo clínico de la FCV-UNLP
L29: # Convocan a perros y gatos con diagnóstico queratosis actínica y carcinoma de células escamosas cutáneo
L30: ## La convocatoria de los investigadores de la Facultad de Ciencias Veterinarias de la Universidad Nacional de La Plata está destinada a pacientes caninos y felinos para participar de un ensayo clínico cuyos objetivos son evaluar aspectos diagnósticos, pronósticos y nuevas alternativas de tratamiento en estas enfermedades.
L31: 
L32: * * *
L33: 
L34: 【8†Image】
L35: 
L36: Foto: FCV-UNLP
L37: Un equipo de investigadores de la Facultad de Ciencias Veterinarias de la Universidad Nacional de La Plata (FCV-UNLP) convoca a pacientes caninos y felinos con lesiones cutáneas pre-malignas -queratosis actínica y/o carcinoma de células escamosas in situ- para participar de un ensayo clínico cuyos objetivos son evaluar aspectos diagnósticos, pronósticos y nuevas alternativas de tratamiento en estas enfermedades.
L38: Esta es una excelente oportunidad para que los tutores de perros y gatos con lesiones cutáneas pre-malignas puedan acceder al diagnóstico y tratamiento de estas lesiones en forma gratuita.
L39: 
L40: El desarrollo de estas lesiones pre-malignas se relaciona con la exposición crónica al sol en áreas de la piel con poco pelo y poco pigmento, y su presencia se asocia con un mayor riesgo de desarrollo de un tipo de cáncer de piel denominado carcinoma de células escamosas cutáneo.
L41: Para poder participar, los tutores de los animales deberán completar un formulario al que se accede desde 【9†aquí†forms.gle】 y en caso de cumplir con los requerimientos serán contactados para coordinar un turno en el Hospital Escuela.
L42: Este estudio se encuentra en el marco del Proyecto de Investigación “Potencial terapéutico de la vía de señalización mTOR en carcinomas de células escamosas cutáneos en caninos y felinos” dirigido por la Doctora Liyare Sanz Ressel, investigadora del Consejo Nacional de Investigaciones Científicas y Técnicas (CONICET) en la FCV-UNLP.

L40: # Dogs with cancer could leave lasting legacy
L41: 
L42: 6 February 2026
L43: 
L44: 【23†Image: A female and male academic kneel down with a cavoodle on the grass】
L45: 
L46: Professor Rachel Allavena and Dr José Granados Soler urge owners of eligible dogs to apply for the trial.
L47: 
L48: (Photo credit: The University of Queensland )
L49: 
L50: A University of Queensland project could be a glimmer of hope for dogs suffering from inoperable or incurable cancers.
L51: The project will test the effectiveness of immunomodulatory drug Enzistat in treating solid tumours caused by naturally occurring cancers, including soft tissue sarcoma, mast cell tumour and melanoma.
L52: 
L53: 【24†Professor Rachel Allavena†veterinary-science.uq.edu.au】 from UQ’s 【25†School of Veterinary Science†veterinary-science.uq.edu.au】 said owners who had been told their dog’s cancer was terminal or their pet’s tumours were inoperable should apply for the trial.
L54: “The 6-week treatment consists of oral tablet Enzistat being administered twice daily, regular consultations, blood samples and biopsies,” Professor Allavena said.
L55: 
L56: “Enzistat is designed to target advanced cancers by activating the patient’s immune system.
L57: 
L58: > “Previous compassionate use trials showed Enzistat achieved tumour regression and increased survival time for palliative patients with advanced, late-stage cancers, supporting further evaluation in a formal trial.
L59: “The research consists of 2 trials with the first focusing on terminal patients where the aim is to prolong their lives.
L60: 
L61: “The second aims to see if the drug can shrink large tumours to allow for surgical removal.”
L62: 
L63: To be eligible for participation, dogs must have received a cancer diagnosis from their vet and be able to provide medical records.
L64: 
L65: Researchers will work with the dogs' regular vet throughout the duration of the trial.
L66: The dogs must also have a predicted survival time of more than 3 months and be able to travel to UQ Gatton at least 3 times over a 6-week period.
L67: 
L68: Solid tumours are a common problem in canine health with approximately 1 in 3 dogs developing cancer in their lifetime.
L69: 
L70: 【26†Dr Jose Granados Soler†uqvets.com.au】 said canine cancers could be treated with surgery, chemotherapy and radiotherapy but expense and availability often prevented dogs receiving treatment.
L71: “Immunotherapeutics is in its infancy in veterinary medicine and is a newly established approach in human oncology,” Dr Granados Soler said.
L72: 
L73: “Our goal is to develop safe, easily applied immunotherapies, amenable to delivery in general practice at an affordable cost.
L74: 
L75: “We will optimise these therapies as sole or combination with standard of care treatments, giving each pet dog the best chance to fight its cancer.”
L76: UQ is undertaking this trial in partnership with drug discovery company Avammune Therapeutics Inc that developed Enzistat.
L77: 
L78: Avammune Therapeutics chief executive Arun Papaiah said beginning the first formal veterinary clinical trial with The University of Queensland was a monumental step.
L79: 
L80: “This trial is not just about advancing science, it’s about providing families more time with their beloved companions,” Mr Papaiah said.
L81: “Enzistat is designed to be an oral, off-the-shelf drug that provides high-end immunotherapy results without the complexity of hospital-based infusions.”
L82: 
L83: The trial will provide Enzistat and research associated assessments, with participants required to cover other veterinary costs.
L84: 
L85: Owners of eligible dogs should apply for the trial by contacting uqvets.sa@uq.edu.au.
